title: This Pear Tallow Balm Is Weirdly Fixing My Spring Skin
body:
Okay so my face feels like a dried-out sponge. You know that feeling? It’s spring, which is supposed to be nice, but the air’s doing this thing where it’s warm one minute and windy the next. My skin has no idea what to do. It’s tight. It’s flaky in weird spots, like right between my eyebrows. But also somehow shiny on my nose. It’s a whole mess. I was just sitting there, scrolling on my phone, and I could feel it. That weird, tight, itchy feeling. Dry spring skin is the worst because you don’t expect it. You’re done with winter, you want to be done with the heavy creams, and then bam. Your face rebels.

Anyway. I got this thing. A tallow balm. Whipped beef tallow balm, to be exact. The scent is Pear. I was, let’s be real, extremely skeptical. Beef fat? For my face? It sounded like something my great-grandmother would have used, not something I’d order online in 2024. But my regular stuff—this expensive gel cream from the fancy store at the mall—wasn’t cutting it. It just sat on top of my skin, all slick and useless. So I figured, why not. The jar showed up, this little thing from an Etsy shop, made in France. I opened it. Smelled like. I don’t know. Nice though. A subtle sweetness, gentle. Not like a candy pear. Just fresh. Fruity but in a quiet way.

I poked it. The texture was weird. Not bad weird. It’s whipped, so it’s like this super dense cloud. You scoop a tiny bit and it melts the second it hits your skin warmth. It doesn’t feel greasy. It just… vanishes. But your skin feels different after. Not shiny. Just like it finally took a drink of water.

## How Beef Tallow Ended Up on My Nightstand

Look, I tried everything first. I had a whole shelf of bottles. Serums in droppers, lotions in pumps, oils in little glass bottles. My bathroom counter looked like a pharmacy. Some of it was fine. Most of it did nothing. A few things made my skin angry and red. I was spending so much money on these tiny bottles of promise. It was exhausting.

Then I kept seeing stuff about tallow skincare. Beef tallow for skin. People talking about it like it was this ancient secret. I read that it’s from grass-fed cows, whipped up, and that it’s weirdly similar to the oils our own skin makes. Our sebum, or whatever. That’s why it absorbs so deep instead of just coating the top. It made a weird kind of sense. If my skin’s barrier is messed up—and with this spring weather, it definitely is—maybe it needs something it actually recognizes. Not a lab-made chemical with a 20-word name.

So I ordered the pear tallow balm. I didn’t tell anyone because it felt a little embarrassing. “What’s that?” “Oh, just rendered cow fat, thanks.” But the jar is cute. It’s simple. It doesn’t look like it came from a farm. It feels substantial in your hand, like you got your money’s worth. I started using it at night, after I washed my face. Just a tiny dab, warmed between my fingers, patted on. The first thing I noticed was my lips. I always have chapped lips. Always. I put the balm on them too. Woke up and they were… normal. Soft. Not cracked. That was the first “huh” moment.

## What This Stuff Actually Does (And Doesn’t Do)

It doesn’t perform miracles overnight. Let’s be clear. It’s not a magic potion. But after about a week, I stopped thinking about my skin. And that’s the real win. I wasn’t feeling that tightness when I smiled. The flaky patch between my brows was just… gone. No more sandpaper cheeks. My skin just felt calm. Hydrated in a way that lotion never managed. Like it was finally satisfied.

It’s become my last step at night. Sometimes in the morning if I’m feeling extra dry. It’s not heavy. You’d think beef tallow balm would be thick and gross, but this whipped version is light. It sinks in. I can put it on and go to bed without feeling like I’m sticking to my pillowcase. My cat jumped on my chest the other night while I had it on and she didn’t even try to lick my face, which is her usual move with scented stuff. So that’s a review from her, I guess.

Here’s an unrelated thing I just remembered: the light in my room at 7 PM this time of year is this specific golden color. It hits the jar on my dresser and the glass looks like honey. I notice it while I’m putting the balm on. It’s a nice little moment. Very peaceful. My skin routine used to be a chore, a series of steps I rushed through. Now it’s just this one thing. Scoop, warm, pat. Done. It’s stupidly simple.

## My Skin Now vs. Spring Skin Two Months Ago

Two months ago, I was using a “spring reset” kit. It had three steps and a toner that smelled like roses and made my eyes water. My skin was confused. It was both oily and peeling. I looked tired all the time. Now? I’m not saying I look like I sleep twelve hours a night. I don’t. I still drink too much coffee. But the texture of my skin is just… better. Even. When I put on makeup, it doesn’t cling to dry patches. It just goes on. My hands get really dry too, from washing them all the time, and I’ve used this on my knuckles. Works better than the thick hand cream I bought at the drugstore.

The pear scent is perfect for spring skincare. It’s not overpowering. It’s just this light, fresh, clean smell that disappears after a minute. It doesn’t compete with perfume or anything. It’s just a nice little experience. I find myself looking forward to putting it on. It feels like a treat, not a treatment. I’m on my second jar now. I got one for my mom, who has super sensitive skin, and she texted me last week saying her winter-damaged elbows haven’t been this smooth in years. High praise.

Would I buy it again? Yeah. I already did. It’s one of the few things I’ve repurchased without even thinking about it. It just works. I don’t know the science. I don’t care about the buzzwords. All I know is my face doesn’t feel like a dried-out sponge anymore. It feels like my face. And in this weird, unpredictable spring weather, that’s a pretty big deal. If your skin is being difficult with the season change, a tallow balm for spring might be worth a shot. I got mine from this little Etsy shop that makes them. No fuss, no crazy packaging. Just a good thing that works.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, weirdly. I thought it would be gross, but it makes sense. It’s similar to the oils our skin already produces, so it gets absorbed deep instead of sitting on top. It’s like giving your skin something it actually recognizes to help repair itself.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not this one, in my experience. It’s non-comedogenic, which means it shouldn’t clog pores. It absorbs really well. It doesn’t feel heavy or greasy at all once it sinks in. My skin feels balanced, not oily.

**What does the Pear tallow balm smell like?**
It’s a subtle sweetness. Like a fresh, ripe pear but not sugary or artificial. It’s light and clean. The smell doesn’t stick around for long, which I like. It’s just a nice little moment when you apply it.

Anyway. My skin’s happy. I’m happy. That’s all I wanted. If you’re curious about trying something different for your dry spring skin, this might be it.
